pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:105 token_endpoint_request POSTs client_secret/refresh material through the unguarded SHARED_HTTP client to a token URL that may come from an OIDC discovery response, and the only private-address guard (validate_issuer_url, oauth.rs:1205) checks IP literals in the string, so a hostname that resolves to loopback or private space passes; the repo's SSRF_SAFE_HTTP is used in the same context (openapi_autopilot.rs:70) but not here.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:105 The discovered token_endpoint is checked only by host-string suffix (validate_endpoint_domain) and the issuer only for IP literals (oauth.rs:1205 `if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<std::net::IpAddr>() {`). No resolved-address judgement or connection binding happens, and both discover_oidc (oauth.rs:1295) and the token POST use SHARED_HTTP. This is exactly the string-check failure the technique names.

src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:267 The OAuth state the browser echoes back is checked against both the per-session value and an instance HMAC (verify_oauth_state, oauth.rs:1466, nonce.timestamp.hmac). A forged state is refused and does not consume the flow.

src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/foraging.rs:725 The webview submits only a foraged id. The backend re-reads the raw values from the source, and the scan result shown to the UI carries only mask_value output (foraging.rs:169).

src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:639 The only listener in this context is a one-shot OAuth callback bound to loopback and gated by the HMAC'd state. It does not serve requests that spend the person's ambient login, so the Host/Origin gate's precondition does not hold. There is no Host check, for the record.

src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:86 The upstream status and body (secret-sanitized at oauth.rs:84) are relayed in the error message, but the only caller is the local operator over IPC, not an anonymous browser caller mapping topology. Under a multi-tenant broker this would be a deviation.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject's techniques assume a web origin serving anonymous visitors. A desktop app whose 'browser' is its own webview (IPC instead of a same-origin route, a user-typed upstream instead of deployment config) needs a stated precondition for opaque-upstream-errors and loopback-addressed-request-gate. Right now a judge has to infer whether 'the caller is the operator' voids them.

declined.subject: browser-credential-boundary
declined.reason: These are input forms for the user's own secrets. The save/encryption path lives in hooks outside the listed files, and nothing in them is a bundle-held credential, a store grant, a broker route or a round-tripped server result. I couldn't anchor five techniques, and couldn't prove absence well enough for a not-applicable verdict to survive the term re-search.
